approved_list.document: Form W-2 from each employer (yours and, if filing jointly, your spouse's), including any employer you left during the year, plus any corrected Form W-2c

Form 1099-R for each distribution, direct rollover, Roth conversion, or pension or annuity payment (RRB-1099-R for railroad retirement tier II), plus proof of the redeposit date and amount for any indirect (60-day) rollover

Form 1099-G, Certain Government Payments, from each agency that paid unemployment (state unemployment agency or Railroad Retirement Board) showing unemployment compensation and any federal income tax withheld

Closing statement from the home purchase (settlement statement, Closing Disclosure, ALTA statement, or HUD-1), including the buyer's side showing points, prorated property taxes, any mortgage insurance or VA funding fee paid at closing, and settlement costs
Provider name, address, taxpayer ID, and amount paid

A copy of the new dependent's Social Security card (name and number as printed) and their date of birth; if the SSN has not been issued, the date it was applied for, or an ATIN (Form W-7A) for a pending adoption, or an ITIN for a dependent who cannot get an SSN; for a child born and died in 2026 without an SSN, a birth certificate, death certificate, or hospital record showing live birth

For each rental real estate property: rents and other amounts received (including the fair market value of any property or services received as rent), expenses paid, the number of days rented at a fair rental price and the number of days of personal use, purchase, improvement, and prior depreciation records, a dated mileage log if car expenses are claimed, and any Forms 1099-MISC or 1099-K received

follow_up_questions.question: Did you itemize deductions on last year's return instead of taking the standard deduction?
